claims.text: Recommended for all patients with diabetes aged 40–75, at moderate–high intensity;
claims.quote: Statins are recommended for all patients with diabetes 40 to 75 years of age (1, 4). Moderate- to high-intensity treatment is used,

claims.text: high-intensity (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin) at higher ASCVD risk.
claims.quote: a high-intensity statin (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin) is recommended for patients at higher ASCVD risk

claims.text: With ASCVD or very high risk, reasonable to target LDL < 70 mg/dL, adding ezetimibe or a PCSK-9 inhibitor if needed.
claims.quote: For all patients with diabetes and established ASCVD or at very high risk for ASCVD, it is also reasonable to target a low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol level < 70 mg/dL (1.81 mol/L) with maximally tolerated statin and addition of ezetimibe or a proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK -9) inhibitor if necessary.

claims.text: MSD: routine LFT monitoring isn't necessary, and routine CK doesn't predict rhabdomyolysis; check muscle enzymes only if myalgias or other muscle symptoms develop.
claims.quote: Routine monitoring of liver enzyme levels is not necessary, and routine measurement of creatine kinase (CK) is not useful to predict the onset of rhabdomyolysis. Muscle enzyme levels need not be checked regularly unless patients develop myalgias or other muscle symptoms.

claims.text: If symptoms don't subside within 1 to 2 weeks off the statin, look for another cause (eg, polymyalgia rheumatica).
claims.quote: If symptoms do not subside within 1 to 2 weeks of stopping the statin, another cause should be sought for the muscle symptoms (eg, polymyalgia rheumatica).

claims.text: Atorvastatin: use with cyclosporine or gemfibrozil is not recommended;
claims.quote: Concomitant use of cyclosporine or gemfibrozil with LIPITOR is not recommended.
claims.locator: 7.1 Drug Interactions that may Increase the Risk of Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis with LIPITOR

claims.text: avoid more than 1.2 L/day of grapefruit juice.
claims.quote: Avoid intake of large quantities of grapefruit juice, more than 1.2 liters daily, when taking LIPITOR.
claims.locator: 7.1 Drug Interactions that may Increase the Risk of Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis with LIPITOR

claims.text: Atorvastatin: tell patients to promptly report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially with malaise or fever.
claims.quote: Instruct patients to promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, particularly if accompanied by malaise or fever.

claims.text: Atorvastatin: discontinue when pregnancy is recognized, or weigh the patient's ongoing need;
claims.quote: Discontinue LIPITOR when pregnancy is recognized. Alternatively, consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the individual patient.
Lactation: Breastfeeding not recommended during treatment with LIPITOR ( 8.2 ).
